title: Responsibility: technology decisions and why to document them

videos.script: Every architecture is a pile of decisions. Most of them were never written down. {{title}} This lesson is about the technology decisions, and about leaving a trail behind them. At Carreto, the Tracking team has to choose where a hundred GPS positions a second will live. {{tracking}} Renata does not pick the winner. She asks six questions. Does it fit? Can the team run it? What would it cost to leave? {{questions}} Then there is the question of how much care a choice deserves. Some decisions are two-way doors. You can walk back through them in an afternoon. Others are one-way doors, and they reach other teams. Those get the architect's attention. {{doors}} One of them is how Payments learns that a delivery was proved. You will read the record for it, whole. Context, decision, consequences, and the options it turned down. {{record}} An accepted record is never edited. When the decision changes, a new record replaces it, and the old reasoning stays readable. {{supersede}} Last, why bother. The engineer who is about to delete a job that looks useless. The meeting that keeps coming back. And the person who decided, judged by what was known at the time. {{why}}
